title: From a rented room to your own house: homes, plots and the house builder in Towneers
html:
Every city game has a moment when you stop being a visitor and start being a resident. In Towneers, a free browser life sim with a shared pixel city, that moment usually has a front door. You begin with a rented apartment, you earn, you save, and one day you walk past a plot with a red SALE sign and think: I could build something here. This guide follows that path from the first rent payment to a house with your name on a plaque at the gate, with the real prices and limits from the game.

Towneers is a free multiplayer cozy sim that runs in the browser on a phone or a computer, with no download. It is in alpha, so numbers can change, and everything below reflects the city as it is now. If you would rather try than read, the game opens in a character editor and you start with 🪙600.

▶ Play Towneers free in your browser

Homes at a glance: three ways to live in the city

You can get a home in Towneers in three ways: rent an apartment or a house, buy one outright, or buy a plot of land and build a house on it yourself. Each path suits a different stage of the game.

  • Rent an apartment. Apartments rent for 🪙44-78 per game day. Rent is not charged below level 5 or during your first 3 days, so the first home is practically free.
  • Buy an apartment or a house. Apartments sell for 🪙4,700-8,200, and houses for 🪙28,200-62,000. A house can also be rented for 🪙133-272 per day if you want a bigger space without the commitment.
  • Buy a plot and build. This is the long road, but it is the only one where the house is truly yours in shape, size, roof and colour.

A home in the game is not just a spawn point. You sleep, shower, cook and store things there, you furnish it with more than 40 kinds of catalogue furniture or pieces crafted by other players, and you can invite friends over. By default friends can come in, and you can change who has access in the home settings.

Step one: the rented room

The first home is the easy one. Walk into a residential building, take the lift to a floor with a FOR RENT door and press "Rent". You can also open the "Housing" app on your phone. Multi-storey buildings in Towneers use lifts, so there is no stair-climbing puzzle: you ride up, find the door and move in.

Renting has a few rules worth knowing:

  • Rent is charged per game day, from 🪙44 to 🪙78 for an apartment.
  • Nothing is charged until level 5, and nothing during your first 3 days.
  • A rented home holds up to 25 of your own furniture items, and heavy pieces such as a hot tub or a pool table are not allowed.

Renting is the right choice while you learn the city. Take a job, try fishing, run a few courier deliveries, and let the money build. If you need a plan for that stage, the beginner guide How to earn your first 1,000 gold covers it.

Step two: buying a flat or a house

When daily rent starts to feel like a leak, the same window offers "Buy". The purchase means no more daily payments, and the home becomes an asset you can sell later. Apartments cost 🪙4,700-8,200 and houses 🪙28,200-62,000.

Owning also raises your furniture limit. An owned home takes up to 60 of your own furniture items, and heavy furniture such as a hot tub or a pool table is allowed. If you like to arrange a space exactly the way you want, that alone is a reason to buy.

Press the furnish button (L on a computer) to enter furnishing mode. You get furniture, wallpaper and floors, so a plain room can become a studio, a cabin or a tiny hangout for friends. Furniture crafted by players can be an alternative to the catalogue, which is one more reason to visit the player market.

Why land matters

An apartment is a room. A plot is a place. Buying land in Towneers changes what the game offers you:

  • You choose the house. Ready-made projects or your own design in the house builder.
  • You get a yard. A garage, a pool, a grill, flower beds, an apple tree and a fence with a gate.
  • You get a face. A plaque at the entrance with your name, and a plot passport that any passer-by can open.
  • You can build more than a home. City plots also take shop pavilions, mixed buildings and apartment complexes for rent income, and North Farms hold farms with a barn and fields.

A player can own up to 4 plots in total. The city has 91 plots, and 38 of them are farm plots, so there is room to choose but not room to hoard.

The three kinds of land and what they cost

Free plots carry a red SALE sign. Walk up to one, or tap it on a phone, and a card opens with a picture, the price, the size, the address and the district. There are three kinds of land.

  • City plots (🪙12,100-34,200). They take houses, shop pavilions, mixed buildings and apartment complexes. Choose these if you want a business next to your home or rental income from an apartment complex.
  • Cottage Hill (🪙19,100-29,500). Quiet streets for houses only. It is the district to pick for a calm home and a pretty street, and a good place for a first house.
  • North Farms (🪙2,700-5,400). The cheapest land, meant for a farm with a barn and fields. Not a place for a mansion, but a great place to grow crops and sell the harvest to city kitchens, the co-op or other players.

Prices depend on the size and the district, and each one is written on the sign. The card also tells you what you can build there, so you never pay for land that does not fit your plan. The real estate agency in the game shows homes and plots for sale and for rent, and the Cottage Hill tour in the game takes you straight to the plots.

Buying the plot

Buying is straightforward: stand at the sign, open the card, check the price and size, and confirm. The plot becomes yours, and it gets a plaque at the entrance. The plot window then offers what you can build on it.

Two practical notes. First, your plot limit is shared: city, Cottage Hill and farm plots all count toward the same 4. Second, if the yard turns out too small, a plot can be expanded to the side from the plot window, so a modest first purchase is not a dead end.

Ready-made or your own: the house builder

After the purchase you have two routes. The plot window offers projects that fit the land, such as the Cosy house and the two-storey Cottage, each with a price and a build time shown. Or you press "Build your own house" and open the house builder.

The builder puts a ghost of your future home above the plot and a Build panel next to it (at the bottom of the screen on a phone). Everything you change shows up on the plot at once, and the price and build time are always visible, so there are no surprises at the till. Your draft saves itself.

What you can design

Here is what the builder lets you choose, as it works in the game today:

  • Size. Width and depth from 3 to 6 tiles, and from 1 to 3 floors.
  • Shape. A simple box, an L-shaped house, a house with a veranda, a house with a garage wing, a house with a turret, or a house made of two volumes. Bigger shapes need more room: a turret needs at least 4 by 4 tiles, for example.
  • Roof. Gable, hip, cross, mansard or shed. Not every roof suits every shape, and the builder only offers combinations that look right.
  • Details. A chimney, dormer windows, a balcony (from two floors up), a weather vane, ivy, a TV glowing in a window and even a cat on the roof.
  • Door side. South, east, north or west, so the house faces the street the way you want.
  • Colours. Wall and roof colours come from the city palette.

The builder also ships with 12 ready templates for a fast start, among them the Cosy house, Cottage, L-house, Tower, Chalet, Cube, Two Levels, a narrow city house, Manor, a U-shaped house and two villas. Pick one, then tweak the roof and colours until it feels like yours.

Price and build time

The builder shows the price and time for your exact design at the bottom of the panel. In general, the cost grows with floor area and floors, and extras add to it: a shape other than a simple box, a roof other than gable or hip, and each detail all cost a little more. Build time follows the same logic, so a tall, wide house with a tower takes longer than a small cabin.

For a sense of scale, the ready-made Cosy house is listed in the game code at 🪙10,500 and 60 minutes. Because the economy is tuned over time, always trust the number on the panel over any number in an article.

Construction, keys and moving in

Once you confirm, scaffolding goes up on the plot right away. When it is done, the keys are yours, and living in your own house is free: no rent, ever.

Moving in is gentle. Your belongings are not lost when you change homes. Things go to your bag or to the storage at the post office, and in the new home a button called "Arrange as before" puts the furniture back where it was.

The interior follows the ground floor of your design: the bigger the house, the roomier the room. A 6 by 6 house gives you real space to furnish; a 3 by 3 cabin is cosy by definition.

Changed your mind? Rebuild

Few players get a house perfect on the first try. "Rebuild" changes the look of the house, meaning shape, roof, details and colours, for a fraction of the price, and your furniture and yard stay where they are. A new position or a new size or number of floors counts as new construction, with its own price and time.

That makes experimenting cheap. Start with a modest house, live in it, and come back to rebuild once you know what you want.

Your plaque, passport and guest book

Every bought plot gets a plaque at the entrance. Press "Set up the plaque" and choose:

  • A name in Latin letters, such as ROSE COTTAGE, up to 16 characters.
  • A motto.
  • A style. Wooden is free. Stone costs 🪙300, a mailbox 🪙450 and wrought iron 🪙600. Gold, neon and crystal styles are sold for Gems.

Anyone can press your plaque to open the plot passport: who lives there, what is built, how well kept the plot is and how many people liked it. Visitors can leave a heart and up to two lines per day in the guest book. You can read the entries, delete any of them, or close the book entirely.

It is a small feature with a big effect. A street with named plots reads like a real neighbourhood, and visitors sign your book the way they would in a holiday cottage.

Decorating the yard

Everything the house does not cover is your yard. Stand on your plot and press the Plot button (L on a computer) to enter yard mode. You will find:

  • Useful things. A shed with 12 storage slots, a grill for cooking outdoors, an outdoor workbench, an apple tree (🪙180) that gives fruit, a well, a hammock and an inflatable pool (🪙650).
  • A garage (🪙3,500). Your car lives at home and drives out right away, and the garage holds two more cars.
  • Decor. Flower beds, trimmed shrubs, a rose arch, a gnome, a pink flamingo, a fountain, a statue, a flagpole and string lights.
  • Fence and ground. A picket fence (🪙400), a hedge (🪙700), stone and more, with a gate at the entrance.

A well-kept yard makes the plot passport shine, and neighbours notice.

Furnishing the interior

Inside, the furnish mode (L) is where the house becomes a home. The catalogue has more than 40 kinds of furniture, and crafters make more, so a living room can come from the shop or from a carpenter you know. A few habits help:

  • Place the bed, kitchen and a sofa first, so the room works before it is pretty.
  • Remember the limit: 25 of your own furniture items when renting, 60 in your own home.
  • Save heavy pieces such as a hot tub or a pool table for the house you own.
  • Invite friends over once you are done. A home with a TV and a sofa is where good evenings begin.

Selling and moving on

At some point you may want to move on. You can sell land, a building or a business to the city for 70% of the estimate, or to players, where the city takes 5%. Moving out never loses items. They go to your bag or the post office storage, and "Arrange as before" restores the layout in the next home.

A cost plan from rent to own house

Here is a realistic staircase, with the real numbers from the game:

  • Stage 1: rent. An apartment for 🪙44-78 per day, free during your first 3 days and below level 5. Earn from jobs and crafts.
  • Stage 2: choose your land. A city plot for 🪙12,100-34,200, a Cottage Hill plot for 🪙19,100-29,500, or a farm plot in North Farms for 🪙2,700-5,400.
  • Stage 3: build. Pick a template or design your own. The price and time are on the panel.
  • Stage 4: the plaque. Free for wood, 🪙300 for stone.
  • Stage 5: the yard. Start with an apple tree (🪙180) and a picket fence (🪙400). Add a pool (🪙650) and a garage (🪙3,500) when you can.
  • Stage 6: rebuild and refresh. Change the roof or the colours for a fraction of the price whenever you like.

You do not have to climb every stair. Some players go from the rented room straight to a farm plot, and others never buy land at all and furnish a rented flat for months.

Five mistakes to avoid

  1. Buying the biggest plot too early. A plot you can afford to build on is better than a big one you cannot. Plots can be expanded later.
  2. Ignoring the zone. Cottage Hill is for houses only, and North Farms is for farms. Check what you can build before you pay.
  3. Spending everything on the plot. Land is not the whole bill. Keep money for construction and a few yard items.
  4. Overbuilding the first design. A turret and three floors cost more and take longer. You can rebuild later for a fraction of the price, so start simple.
  5. Forgetting the plaque. It is free in wood, and it turns a plot into a place people can visit, like and sign.

Questions and answers

How much does a house cost in Towneers?

You can rent a house for 🪙133-272 per game day or buy one for 🪙28,200-62,000. If you buy land and build, you pay for the plot plus the build price shown in the builder.

Can I build my own house design?

Yes. Buy a plot, open the plot window and press "Build your own house". You choose size, floors, shape, roof, details, door side and colours.

How big can the house be?

Between 3 and 6 tiles in width and depth, and from 1 to 3 floors.

How many plots can I own?

Up to 4 per player, counting city, Cottage Hill and farm plots together.

Can I change the house after it is built?

Yes. "Rebuild" changes shape, roof, details and colours for a fraction of the price, and your furniture and yard stay. A new position, size or number of floors is new construction.

Do I pay rent in my own house?

No. Once the house is built, living there is free.

What happens to my furniture when I move?

Nothing is lost. Items go to your bag or the post office storage, and "Arrange as before" restores the layout in the new home.

Who can see my plaque and yard?

Everyone. Any player can open the plot passport, leave a like and write in the guest book, unless you close it.

Can friends visit my home?

Yes. Friends can come in by default, and you can change access in the home settings.

How do I sell a house or a plot?

Sell it to the city for 70% of the value, or to another player, where the city takes 5%.

Is Towneers free?

Yes. It is a free browser game with no time limits and no download, and it works on a phone, tablet or computer. Optional purchases such as Gems and Premium exist.

Can I play on a phone?

Yes. The builder panel moves to the bottom of the screen on a phone.

Where do I get the money for a plot?

From jobs, crafts, fishing, farming or your own business. The guide How to earn your first 1,000 gold is a good start.

Your turn

A rented room is a fine beginning, and a house with your name on the gate is a fine goal. Towneers lets you build your own house online in a shared pixel city, with friends who can sign your guest book and neighbours down the street. Pick a plot, sketch your house and see how it looks from the road. For the short version, see the game guide on homes or the blog guide Your plot and house: from purchase to plaque.
